pool.text: Nestorian Christians became essentially extinct in China by this specific year.
Previous maritime intendancies of Guangzhou were closed, limiting legal trade.
Rafael Perestrello traveled to Guangzhou as a passenger on a native junk.
Leonel de Sousa legalized Portuguese trade through the Luso-Chinese Accord.
Zhu Yuyue fled by sea to Guangzhou, the last Ming stronghold.
Ming turncoat Li Chengdong sacked the city on behalf of the Qing.
Chiang solidified his control over the Nationalists during the Canton Coup.
The Canton Operation subjected the city to Japanese occupation.
Guangzhou was captured by military forces.
The Canton Fair was inaugurated as a major event for the city.
The first line of the Guangzhou Metro opened, creating an underground railway system.
Baiyun International Airport officially opened for operation in Baiyun District.
Thousands of buses and taxis operated using LPG fuel at this time.
The municipal government enforced a strict ban on motorcycles in urban areas.
The Wuhan-Guangzhou high-speed railway started active service connecting distant regions.
Guangzhou hosted the notable Asian Games and Asian Para Games.
The library fully opened its doors in a new Zhujiang New Town building.
Luogang merged into Huangpu and counties were upgraded to districts.
The Guiyang-Guangzhou high-speed railway and Nanning-Guangzhou railway began operational service.
Terminal 2 of the major international airport officially opened to passengers.
